To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully demonstrated a working prototype of a dataflow inspired multi grain execution model on a hybrid hardware platform that is capable of executing dataflow programs with a performance overhead that is comparable to that of traditional multi grained execution models.

we have developed the computational tools to implement dataflow inspired fine grained synchronization schemes within a dataflow runtime system and applied it to a face landmark estimation application.
the proposed hardware software co design is capable of achieving a 3.4x performance gain over a traditional x86 based implementation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: 1. How can we use the hybrid architecture of embedded system boards to emulate the fine grained dataflow synchronization mechanisms found in PXMs?

the exploration and development of a hardware software co designed platform which implements the Dataflow inspired PXMs in a way that can be applied to the development and implementation of AI algorithms.

the exploration of the potential synergies between the Dataflow and the Brain inspired execution models and the potential benefits of a software hardware co designed platform to support the development of dataflow inspired PXMs and architectures for AI applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a platform for experimentation and evaluation of dataflow PXMs on a hybrid architecture.
the DEMAC platform provides a unique opportunity to investigate the benefits of the fine grain dataflow synchronization schemes when applied to a brain inspired algorithm.
the DEMAC platform is an ideal platform to experiment, develop and test dataflow inspired PXMs and their corresponding hardware software co design solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a software hardware co designed platform that can be used for the exploration of dataflow based multi grained PXMs.

we have successfully demonstrated the benefits of a hybrid architecture that combines the benefits of a dataflow execution model, a programmable logic system, an embedded system board with multicore processors and a 3D printed Beowulf cluster to implement a dataflow inspired execution model for brain inspired algorithms and applications.
we have developed a dataflow runtime system and a dataflow PXM based on the Codelet Model and implemented the dataflow PXM in a hybrid architecture that is based on the DEMAC platform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to achieve significant speedup over traditional CPU implementations by exploiting data parallelism and fine grain parallelism through dataflow PXMs.
we have demonstrated that the DEMAC platform is capable of supporting the Codelet Model and its associated runtime system.
we can achieve the desired performance of a fine grained dataflow PXM on a commodity hardware architecture.
